section: Verifying while the dev server runs
sentence: `blume build` and `[MASK]` regenerate the _same_ `.blume/`, so running either while the dev server is live would corrupt it — both refuse with an error and exit non-zero:   The `--isolated` flag is the escape hatch.
`[MASK]` — write the files but skip the dependency install, for CI or custom dependency workflows.
`blume init --eject` — scaffold, then eject to a standalone Astro project (with `--no-install`, falls back to guiding you through `[MASK]` once dependencies are installed).
The JSON report carries the same `[MASK]` + `summary` shape as `blume validate --json`, `blume audit --json`, and `blume eval --json`, with the drift grouped per locale.

`[MASK]` closes that loop: it computes exactly which pages are missing or stale in each locale, translates them headlessly with a local agent CLI, and records what it did in a committed ledger so the next run — and CI — knows what's current.

With `--json`, `blume validate` (and [`blume doctor`](/docs/cli/doctor)) write one object to stdout: a `diagnostics` list, each entry carrying its `code`, `severity`, `message`, the `file` relative to the project root with `line` and `column` when the finding has a location, a `[MASK]`, and a `docsUrl` pointing at the page that explains the code, plus a `summary` of counts per severity.
The first cut turns versioning on, adding a `[MASK]` block with the id archived and the live docs labeled "Latest".

That covers inline links and images, reference-style definitions (`[x]: /guides/x`), and HTML `href` and `src` attributes in either quote style, and a link that spells out your [`basePath`](/docs/deployment#mount-the-docs-under-a-path) keeps it (`/docs/guides/x` becomes `[MASK]`).
**Rewrites root-absolute links inside the copy** so they stay within the snapshot: `/guides/x` becomes `[MASK]`.

Each adapter owns its model, the env var its key is read from, how it maps [reasoning](#reasoning), and which provider SDK it needs — so there is no shared set of fields to reconcile across backends:    `openai()`, `anthropic()`, `[MASK]`, and `grok()` call the provider's own API with your key — nothing sits in between.
`PageFooter` renders at the foot of every page Blume builds from your content, API operation pages included, with `[MASK]` and `Pagination` after it.

On a [multilingual](/docs/content/i18n#per-locale-navigation) site, `copyright` and a `[MASK]` can each be a map of locale code to text, and an internal link moves into the reader's locale whenever that locale serves the page.
Set `[MASK]`** to show the mark alone — handy when the logo image already includes the wordmark.

It defaults to the long form (`[MASK]`, `2026年7月21日`):   `dateFormat` is a pass-through to [`Intl.DateTimeFormat`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/DateTimeFormat/DateTimeFormat) options.

The brand is a mark (`image`) plus a wordmark (`text`); the object form lets you set them independently:   `image` takes the same value as the shorthand — a single path, or `{ light, dark, alt }` for separate light/dark artwork (raster images must live in `[MASK]`).

It follows renames, as `git log --follow` does: renaming `page.md` to `[MASK]`, or moving a file to another folder under the same content root, keeps the page's date as long as the commit leaves its content unchanged.
Before it generates anything, the build logs how many new clips it needs and how many characters they cover, so the cost is visible up front:   `[MASK]` takes:

`openai()` generates the clips with OpenAI's speech API instead: OpenAI's own models with your `[MASK]`, or, with a `baseUrl`, any server that serves the same `POST /audio/speech` endpoint, such as [Kokoro-FastAPI](https://github.com/remsky/Kokoro-FastAPI), [Speaches](https://speaches.ai), or a [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai) proxy with a speech model.
Run `blume build` and `[MASK]` to hear the generated voice locally.
Without `apiKeyEnv`, a `[MASK]` server is called with no key, so your `OPENAI_API_KEY` never leaves for another server.
Leave `[MASK]` unset when readers reach the server directly.
`[MASK]` lists extra terms the page is found by, even when its text doesn't use them.
`Esc` closes it, and `[MASK]` (or `Ctrl J`) toggles the result preview pane.
Optional props (`[MASK]` unset) show a `?` after the name.

`[MASK]` keeps the page out of [`llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`](/docs/discoverability/llms-txt#excluding-a-page) and out of the page map in your [site's skill](/docs/discoverability/agent-discovery#your-sites-skill).
`[MASK]` multiplies the page's relevance: above 1 ranks it higher, below 1 lower.

Changelog entries (`type: changelog`) accept an optional `changelog` object for richer feed and display metadata:   `[MASK]` may live here or at the top level — both feed the [changelog RSS feed](/docs/content#feeds).
`[MASK]` keeps the page out of search, and `tags` labels its record for a hosted search adapter to filter on (see [Tags](/docs/configuration/search#tags)).
The default (Orama) and FlexSearch indexes filter in the browser, Pagefind keeps an index per language, and Algolia, Orama Cloud, and Typesense carry a `[MASK]` field on each record.
In CI, `[MASK]` fails when a source page has drifted ahead of its translations.
Other HTML there has to be valid JSX: an `` or `[MASK]` without a closing slash takes in everything after it in the partial, with no error.
Blume generates an RSS feed automatically for each content type listed in [`seo.rss.types`](/docs/discoverability/rss) — `blog` and `[MASK]` by default — as long as it has at least one page.

Instead, `blume/hooks` reads a small snapshot the layout serializes into the page — no props to drill:    `[MASK]` and `usePage()` return `null` until the island mounts (so server and client render the same first frame) — guard for it.
Blume warns about that one as `BLUME_META_OUTSIDE_INCLUDE`: add an `[MASK]` glob that reaches the folder, such as `"api/**/*.{md,mdx}"`, so Blume reads it.
The `[MASK]` array lists children by slug — the folder or file name with its numeric prefix and any parentheses stripped (so `01-quickstart.mdx` is `"quickstart"`).
It's on by default; hide it with `[MASK]`:   The link only appears when `github` is configured, so projects without a repo are unaffected either way.

The setting carries down to nested folders, so one `directory` on the content root's `[MASK]` gives every section a listing, and a folder can set its own value (`none` included) to override what it inherits.

On a route under no tab (or a tab whose `[MASK]` is `/`), the sidebar shows the pages that _don't_ belong to a tab — each tab's folder is hidden from it, since that section already has its own tab in the header.
A section whose `[MASK]` isn't a page of its own — a folder with no `index.mdx` — would link to a 404, so the tab falls back to the first page in the section instead.
Its `path` still scopes the sidebar and marks the tab as current, and `[MASK]` doesn't apply.
A path to a file in `public/` (`/spec.pdf`) or one Blume generates (`[MASK]`) matches too.
Under `--preview` the adapter reads drafts through the Preview API with `[MASK]`.
`custom()` takes a `[MASK]` instance rather than an options object, so there is nothing to pass the [shared options](/docs/content/sources#adapters) `prefix` or `pollInterval` to.
`[MASK]` serves that snapshot after you edit the source's query, fields, or serializers, so run `blume sync` to fetch afresh.
For a repository on GitHub Enterprise Server, set `baseUrl` to its REST API (`https://<host>/api/v3`); `[MASK]` is sent there, so it must be a token for that server.

Beyond `[MASK]`, each built-in adapter has its own page, and [`custom()`](/docs/content/sources/custom) plugs in any other backend:   Every adapter that takes an options object accepts two shared options:  `prefix`** namespaces the source's routes under `/<prefix>/…`, which also becomes the source's name in diagnostics and its cache directory.
The top-level `[MASK]`, `content.include`, and `content.exclude` options are shorthand for that single source — nothing to import, nothing to change.

Two flags control how remote content is fetched and what's included:  `--preview`** on `blume dev` or `[MASK]` renders drafts and pulls unpublished CMS content — Sanity switches to its `previewDrafts` perspective, Contentful reads through the Preview API, and Payload and Strapi request drafts.
Run `blume sync` to pull the latest content (a running dev server hot-reloads), or `[MASK]` to drop the snapshots first.
When `sources` is present it replaces the implicit default, so include a `[MASK]` entry for your local docs — and move `root`, `include`, or `exclude` into it.

Preview and published content get separate snapshots, and so does each set of source options, so a build never falls back to drafts fetched under `--preview`, and editing a source's `[MASK]` or `fields` fetches afresh.
The `[MASK]` property is a publish gate by default.
`[MASK]` is dropped rather than resolved — alias link targets are not supported yet.
The API key comes from the `[MASK]` environment variable and is sent as `users API-Key <key>`; set `authCollection` when the key belongs to another auth-enabled collection.

Enumerate files either from a GitHub repo subtree (`[MASK]`) or explicitly against a raw base URL (`url` + `files`):   To list the files yourself, point `url` at a raw base URL:   `include` (default `["**/*.{md,mdx}"]`) filters the files by their path under `path`, the way a `filesystem()` source's `include` does: a pattern starting with `!` excludes what it matches (`["**/*.mdx", "!drafts/**"]`).

GitHub caps the listing (100,000 entries or 7 MB for the whole repository, whatever `[MASK]` is), and past it the source warns with `BLUME_SOURCE_TRUNCATED`: list the files with `url` and `files` instead.
The built-in `[MASK]` adapter fetches raw `.md`/`.mdx` over HTTP.
The adapter declares `[MASK]` as its runtime dependency — an optional peer, so install it only if you use this source.
Entries are fetched with `populate=*` so images carry their URLs (set `populate` to narrow it), and a relative upload path (`/uploads/x.png`) in a Blocks field resolves against `[MASK]`.
A `<Badge>` in a heading is a label, not part of that text: `## Install <Badge>beta</Badge>` anchors as `[MASK]` and reads "Install" in the table of contents.
Spaces inside the braces are fine (`[MASK]`).

Add a `versions` block naming the current docs and any archived snapshots:   `current` labels the unprefixed tree in the switcher (with an optional `[MASK]`).
The dev server's header lists only what it serves — the `service-desc` and `alternate` links — because `blume build` writes the catalogs, `agent-readability.json`, and `[MASK]` into the build output.

The catalog and its `[MASK]` neighbors (the API catalog, the MCP discovery files) are served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on every build surface, so a registry reading them from another origin isn't blocked.
The knobs live under two keys in `[MASK]`: `seo` for what search engines and social platforms see, and `agents` for what agents see.
Every generated file yields to one you ship yourself: drop a `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt`, `[MASK]`, or `agent-readability.json` in `public/` and Blume serves yours in its place.

Errors are [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) problem details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `[MASK]`, a `detail`, and a `resolution` hint telling the agent where to go next — a missing page, a blank search query, or on server output any `/api/…` URL no endpoint answers:
`[MASK]`** — the entire corpus: each page's full Markdown body, with its source URL, in one file.

To keep an individual page out of both files, set `[MASK]` in its frontmatter:   The page still renders, stays in search, and keeps its place in the sitemap — only the `llms.txt` files and the page map in your [site's skill](/docs/discoverability/agent-discovery#your-sites-skill) skip it.
Append `.md` or `[MASK]` to any page's URL to fetch its raw Markdown source — perfect for LLMs, coding agents, and "copy as Markdown" workflows.
Send `[MASK]` without a q-value to get Markdown everywhere.
`[MASK]` and `resources/read` still return a hidden page by its route: hidden isn't private, and the page is still served at its URL and as Markdown.
It suits site-verification tokens from Google, Bing, or Facebook, a `[MASK]`, or an app banner:   Each key is the tag's name and each value its content.
`[MASK]` and `og:url` — the page's absolute URL (when [`deployment.site`](/docs/deployment) is set).
Open Graph families (`og:`, `[MASK]`, `article:`, and the rest) render with `property`, as the protocol names them, and everything else with `name`.
For anything Blume has no setting for, add tags under `[MASK]` and every page carries them, custom pages and API references included.
An explicit `og.fonts: []` opts out entirely: cards keep the built-in font even when `[MASK]` is set or a title needs a script fallback.
Blume builds an RSS feed for each content type in `[MASK]` — `blog` and `changelog` by default — that has pages, served at `/<type>/rss.xml`.
`[MASK]` and `sitemap: {}` keep alternates off; `sitemap: false` turns the sitemap off.

When docs live inside another site (`example.com/docs`), point at the entities that site already defines instead of defining them again:   Every page names `[MASK]` as its `isPartOf`, and Blume stops emitting its own WebSite node, whose name and URL would describe the docs instead of the site.
A custom page has no content file to date, so pass `lastModified` to give it a `[MASK]`.
Eject** — `[MASK]` produces a standalone Astro project that still uses the `blume` package.

Without `[MASK]`, pages send no credentials.
`auth` is how requests authenticate unless a page sets `authMethod`: `method` is `bearer`, `basic`, `key`, or `[MASK]`, and `name` is the header an API key goes in (`x-api-key` by default).
Path parameters are written in braces, `[MASK]`, and filled from the matching `path` field.
Each entry in `[MASK]` renders one schema on its own route.
The `[MASK]` is the live GraphQL API URL.
That makes `[MASK]` required for a working proxy: without one, the proxy has no origin to allow for this reference and refuses every send (the build warns about this).

`[MASK]` starts nested schema rows expanded rather than collapsed:   Every sample is plain, copy-pasteable code for the request, written with the language's standard or most common HTTP client:   Each value is quoted by its own language's rules, so a header like `If-Match: "33a64df5"` or a body with a `$` in it reaches the API as written.
The one key that can't be forwarded is Scalar's own multi-document `[MASK]`: that name is Blume's, and each Blume source becomes its own page.
